OBJECTIVES
- Build a Kuberbetes cluster using all your Raspberry Pi’s as nodes (the minimum number
of Pi’s is equal to the number of members in your group) and your own notebooks as
Masters (controllers). The number of controllers is up to you. You may choose to use
wired or wireless connectivity, but wired is preferred especially during demo.
- Find/build an application to deploy on your cluster. Your application must use at least
n different container images providing distinct services (the minimum number of
container images is equal to the number of members in your group). You may choose
any application architecture: monolithic or microservice.
- The containers must be dependent on each other, meaning that a client request must
be serviced by at least 2 different containers before a response is sent back to the
client. This requires networking containers on different nodes (yet another application
of SDN).
- Your application must be fault-tolerant in that if any single node (Raspberry Pi) and its
containers go offline, your system will generate replacements and your application will
automatically continue to work after the replacements are up and running. (The app

automatically continue to work after the replacements are up and running. (The app
can fail until the point where the replacements are running).

APPLICATION CONSIDERATIONS
- If you chose a microservices architecture for your
application, the way you break up your services needs to
“make sense”, i.e., be logical and practical. Do not break
things up just for the sake of this project.
- A stateless application is the easiest choice for this project.
A stateful application will require more effort. Think about
why and design your application wisely.
- You may chose to implement a simple stateless application,
as long as the application logic and services make sense.
